as_told.title: Vallée's Passport to Magonia: the same phenomenon wearing cultural masks
as_told.place_text: Europe; Celtic lands; Ellsworth missile base, South Dakota

plain: Old stories of fairies and elves are said to match modern alien abduction stories closely, an idea from the researcher Jacques Vallée in his book Passport to Magonia. The writer Graham Hancock lays it out: in the old tales, fairies and elves "would do surgery on people," abduct them, have sex with them and produce hybrid babies, just as in abduction accounts, and he links this to his own book Supernatural. Michels, in a later episode, calls Passport to Magonia a great book whose argument was "heretical to both believers and debunkers," framing it as the same phenomenon wearing different cultural masks over time. He applies it to a 1977 case at Ellsworth involving Air Force veterans who say they were abducted. If true, fairies and aliens would be one thing seen through different eras.
